blocks.text: This is the most widespread terrestrial ecosystem of the plains in Pakistan. It is characterized by xerophytic (drought-resistant) plants with thorns to deter herbivores and reduce water loss.

items: Location: The Indus Plains, covering much of Punjab (Bahawalpur, Khanewal, Mianwali, Dera Ghazi Khan), Sindh (southern regions bordering the Indus River), and Balochistan (western regions).
Abiotic Profile: Climate: Arid to semi-arid; summer temperatures can reach 50°C.
Water: Scanty rainfall (200 mm to 750 mm annually).
Key Flora: Prosopis cineraria (Jhand/Kandi), Salvadora oleoides (Peelu/Wan), and Capparis aphylla (Karir) and Vachellia nilotica (Kikar).
Key Fauna: Camels, houbara bustard, chinkara, golden jackal, Balochistan gerbil, porcupines, and rattlesnakes.
Current Status: Heavily Degraded. Most of these "natural jungles" have been cleared for human settlements and the massive canal-irrigation agriculture of the Punjab.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book lists rattlesnakes among the animals of the tropical thorn forest, but rattlesnakes live only in the Americas; a typical venomous snake of Pakistan's thorn forests is the saw-scaled viper (Echis carinatus).

blocks.alt: A dry plains scene with thorny trees and shrubs on grassy slopes. Labelled: a camel on the far ridge, a chinkara grazing under a tree, a porcupine by rocks, a coiled snake on a dry patch, Balochistan gerbils in the grass and karir shrubs with red flowers.
